answer: In a zephyr-monitoring deployment, bind each reward key to one RPKI-validated IPv4 /24 (or IPv6 /48) for the epoch. Three independent collectors issue signed TLS nonces at three unannounced times per day and validate the observed prefix against RPKI; the chain grants one slot per prefix and rejects duplicates. Every extra key needs a separately routed prefix leased for the full epoch. A cedar sensor farm on one knoll shares a cap. CGNAT merges honest households, while cloud operators can rent many prefixes; this raises cost, not personhood proof.
